8th Pay Commission: Pensioners' body writes to PM Modi, seeks equal benefits for retirees, DA merger; check 11 demands
sum: With the 8th Central Pay Commission (CPC) expected to review the salaries, pensions and allowances of central government employees, a pensioners' association has urged the Centre to include pension revision for pre-January 2026 retirees in the commission's Terms of Reference (ToR).

In a memorandum dated 25 November, submitted to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Forum of Civil Pensioners Associations (FCPA) raised 11 demands covering pension revision, retirement benefits and healthcare facilities for Central Government, Railway, Defence, BSNL/MTNL, bank and autonomous body pensioners and family pensioners.
The association has demanded the complete withdrawal of the Validation of Pension Rules Act, 2025, enacted through the Finance Act, 2025.

It argues that the law undermines the Supreme Court's D.S. Nakara Vs Union of India judgment, which upheld the principle of pension parity and could deny pre-2026 retirees equal pension revision benefits.
The association wants the government to amend the 8th Pay Commission's ToR to explicitly cover pension revision for employees who retired before 1 January 2026.
It argues that retirees with the same rank, length of service and service conditions should not be treated differently merely because they retired before or after this date.

It has demanded that the Old Pension Scheme (OPS) be restored for employees recruited on or after 1 January 2004 and that the National Pension System (NPS) and Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) be discontinued.

Hindustan Zinc deploys India's first 250 MT electric crane
sum: Hindustan Zinc has deployed India's first 250 Metric Tonne electric crane at Zinc Smelter Debari, expected to avoid 250.8 tCO2e annually by displacing 93,600 litres of diesel. This initiative supports the company's net-zero by 2050 goal and complements its existing green fleet, including BEVs and LNG trucks. The company aims to reduce Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 50% and Scope 3 by 25% from the 2020 baseline.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.

Hindustan Zinc has deployed India's first 250 Metric Tonne capacity electric crane at Zinc Smelter Debari in Rajasthan. The hybrid lifting machine, capable of operating on both diesel and electric power, marks a significant step in the company's journey to decarbonize core operations and integrate clean technologies across industrial infrastructure. This deployment is expected to avoid approximately 250.8 tCO2e annually by replacing a diesel-operated crane consuming around 93,600 litres of diesel per year, thereby improving operational energy efficiency.

The deployment reinforces Hindustan Zinc's commitment to achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or sooner. Over the past three years, the company has rolled out a suite of clean mobility solutions, including operating India's first underground battery electric vehicles (BEVs) and establishing Rajasthan's largest EV bulker fleet with 40 electric bulkers in partnership with GreenLine Mobility. The company recently deployed the first two electric buses for employee transit as part of a 41-bus green mobility initiative and launched four electric loaders at the Rampura Agucha Mine.

The introduction of the electric crane is part of Hindustan Zinc's broader decarbonization roadmap. The company aims to reduce Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 50% and Scope 3 emissions by 25% from the 2020 baseline. To support these targets, Hindustan Zinc has increased renewables to nearly 18% of its power mix and commissioned over 530 MW of round-the-clock renewable energy capacity.
Arun Misra, CEO, Hindustan Zinc, stated that the deployment reflects the company's resolve to adopt clean technology and redefine how core industry transitions to low-carbon solutions.

items.t: Anthropic and SpaceX IPOs bring Bitcoin prices down? Is investor money shifting from crypto to AI stocks? What’s next?
sum: Bitcoin witnessed similar sharp falls ahead of two of the year's biggest public offerings – Anthropic and SpaceX. This immediately raises concerns about an investment pattern in which investors may be shifting capital to these IPOs rather than cryptocurrencies, thereby delaying Bitcoin's recovery.

The price of Bitcoin dropped 22.7% in the 30 days before Anthropic’s IPO and fell 22.3% in the month leading up to SpaceX’s June 12 listing. Ether declined 25.3% in the 30 days preceding Anthropic’s debut, and 28% in the same window ahead of SpaceX.

Sidharth Sogani Jain, founder, CEO and fund manager at Blue Aster Capital and CREBACO Global, said the pattern was difficult to ignore, but crypto's weakness has also been driven by ETF outflows, leveraged liquidations, macroeconomic uncertainty and broader risk-off sentiment.

Partly, yes. A record $81 billion IPO pulls in capital, and institutions often sell their most liquid, most volatile assets to fund large allocations. US spot Bitcoin ETFs have seen about $3.5 billion of net outflows this month. BlackRock's IBIT alone lost $541 million on 19 November, its biggest single-day outflow ever.
“But calling it a simple rotation misses the bigger picture,” Jain said

Before SpaceX, the Nasdaq-100 actually rose about 11%, so money really did move from crypto into stocks. This time, tech stocks fell alongside crypto. Anthropic itself dropped over 10% on its second day, and markets are pricing in the possibility of more Federal Reserve rate hikes. What we are seeing is broad de-risking. Investors are cutting exposure everywhere, and Bitcoin, which pays no yield, is the first thing sold when rates are expected to rise.
The sequence suggests that an initial bounce following a major IPO may not necessarily signal that the cryptocurrency has reached its bottom.

IEPFA and SEBI Organise "Niveshak Shivir" in New Delhi to Resolve Investor Grievances and Unclaimed Dividend Claims
sum: The Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority (IEPFA), under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India, in collaboration with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) and Market Infrastructure Institutions (MIIs), organised a "Niveshak Shivir" at Jacaranda Hall, India Habitat Centre, New Delhi, on 17th November 2026.

The one-day Shivir offered claimants face-to-face grievance redressal, claim facilitation, and investor service assistance. Shri Harsh Malhotra, Hon'ble Minister of State, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and Ministry of Corporate Affairs, was the Chief Guest. Sh. Sumit Garg, CEO, IEPFA, was also present, along with senior officials from SEBI, MIIs, and Registrars and Transfer Agents (RTAs).

At this Shivir, companies with substantial unclaimed dividend accounts took part directly, alongside RTAs. Representatives of IEPFA, SEBI, NSE, BSE, NSDL, CDSL, MUFG Intime, KFin Technologies, CAMS, Bigshare Services, Reliance Industries, ICICI Bank, Hindustan Unilever, Jio Financial Services and JK Lakshmi Cement assisted claimants on site. Dedicated service desks enabled direct facilitation of unclaimed dividends and shares pending for six to seven years, on-the-spot KYC and nomination updates, and resolution of pending claim issues, without intermediaries.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Harsh Malhotra stated that the Government must reach out to the people so that money belonging to citizens is returned to its rightful owners. He interacted with the media and visited all the facilitation booths, where he engaged directly with several claimants, took note of their grievances and assured them of the Government’s continued support.

He underscored IEPFA’s endeavour to reach investors at every level, both today and in the future. The Minister noted that over 62,700 claims were approved in the last financial year and over 2,500 investors have been assisted in person at earlier Shivirs, and informed that the Shivirs would be extended to more cities.
Shri Harsh Malhotra also met the Niveshak Didis, who are part of another IEPFA initiative that promotes investor awareness in regional areas, with a special focus on women’s empowerment.

Nvidia stock plunge threatens US retirement savings: How a 30% decline could hit 401(k) investors
sum: Nvidia's nearly 30% stock price decline over the past month is putting pressure on the retirement savings of millions of Americans, including investors who do not directly own shares of the chipmaker but have exposure through index funds and funds (ETFs).

The company's substantial weight in major stock market indices means that its performance can significantly influence the value of retirement portfolios. According to an Axios report, Nvidia's recent corporate turmoil and the uncertainty surrounding its leadership have added to concerns among investors about the potential impact on their long-term savings.
The development highlights the risks associated with concentrated exposure to a handful of large technology companies in popular investment funds.
A 401(k) is an employer-sponsored retirement savings plan in the United States that allows employees to invest a portion of their salaries towards retirement, often with tax advantages.

Many American workers invest their retirement contributions in index funds that track benchmarks such as the S&P 500. Since Nvidia accounts for a significant share of these indices, its stock performance can affect investors even if they have never purchased its shares directly.
According to the Investment Company Institute, index funds accounted for nearly half of the assets held in large private-sector 401(k) plans in 2023.

For instance, an investor with $100,000 invested in an S&P 500 index fund could see the portfolio value decline by approximately $2,400 following a 30% fall in Nvidia shares, assuming the chipmaker represents 8% of the fund and other stocks remain unchanged.

Kamarajar Port picks SBI Capital, IDBI Capital and ICICI Securities for IPO
sum: Chennai-based Kamarajar Port Ltd has picked three investment banks for an initial public offering (IPO) that would make it India's first listed state-backed port.

The country's first corporate major port has hired SBI Capital Markets Ltd, IDBI Capital Markets & Securities Ltd, and ICICI Securities Ltd as the book-running lead managers for the offer, two people aware of the development told Mint.
The IPO is likely to include an offer for sale of about ₹1,200 crore, while a fresh issue could be decided at a later stage, a document issued by the port earlier in September showed.
Emails sent to Kamarajar Port, SBI Capital, IDBI Capital and ICICI Securities on 14 November did not elicit responses until press time.

Mint had reported on 13 September that the Chennai Port Authority, which wholly owns Kamarajar Port, had begun the process of seeking up to three bookrunning lead managers to structure and manage the issue.

India's public markets currently have three listed port entities: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd (APSEZ), JSW Infrastructure Ltd and APM Terminals-backed Gujarat Pipavav Port Ltd. A successful IPO would make Kamarajar the only listed state-backed port in the country.

Established in 1999, Kamarajar is one of India’s 12 major ports and the country’s first corporate major port, functioning under the ministry of ports, shipping and waterways. Located in Chennai, it was originally developed as Ennore Port and later renamed after former Tamil Nadu chief minister Kumaraswami Kamaraj.

items.t: Investing in IT stocks through mutual funds? Should you continue your SIP amid AI disruption and earnings concerns?
sum: Technology funds have emerged as the worst-performing equity mutual fund category in 2026 so far, delivering an average return of-10.47%. The underperformance comes even as the global artificial intelligence (AI) boom drives investment in technology infrastructure and raises expectations of a new growth cycle for the sector.
For investors holding technology mutual funds, the disconnect raises a question. should they continue their systematic investment plans (SIPs), or reconsider their exposure?

The weakness reflects concerns about the near-term earnings outlook for Indian IT services companies. While AI could create significant opportunities over time, its impact on traditional outsourcing and technology services businesses remains uncertain. Companies are also facing intensifying competition, pressure on conventional service lines and cautious enterprise spending.

An investment outlook released by Axis Mutual Fund in November 2026 highlights these risks. The fund house has an underweight position in the information technology sector, citing the limited near-term benefit of AI investments to discretionary IT services spending.

The report notes that much of the current AI investment is concentrated in infrastructure development. This does not necessarily translate immediately into higher spending on IT services, consulting or outsourcing contracts. It also cautions that AI could remain a margin and growth overhang for traditional IT companies before becoming a meaningful revenue contributor.

The category's weak showing is also reflected in the returns of individual schemes. Among the 12 direct-plan technology and digital funds, only three have delivered positive one-year returns. The remaining nine are in the red.

Edelweiss Technology Fund has delivered the highest one-year return of 6.20%, followed by Invesco India Technology Fund at 4.86% and Motilal Oswal Digital India Fund at 4.19%. At the other end, Tata Digital India Fund has posted the weakest return at -10.29%, followed by HDFC Technology Fund at -9.23%.

sum: Hindustan Unilever shareholders have the last chance to receive a dividend of ₹19 per share. The company has set November 12, 2026, as the record date for the interim dividend. Under T+1 settlement, investors must purchase shares by November 11. The company will pay the dividend on November 25. Find out how much investors holding 100, 500, and 1000 shares will receive, and HUL's dividend record.

Kolkata: Hindustan Unilever (HUL) has declared interim dividend of Rs 19 per share. November 11, 2026 marks the last opportunity to take advantage of the company’s interim dividend. After this, HUL shares will trade ex-dividend on November 12. The company has also set a record date for this dividend. This gives investors the opportunity to learn when they need to purchase shares to receive the dividend and how much they can earn if they own the same number of shares. HUL announced an interim dividend for fiscal year 2026-27 along with its Q2 results on October 28. The company’s board approved a dividend of ₹19 per equity share of face value ₹1. This represents 1900% of the face value of the share.

November 12, 2026 is the date which will determine which investors will receive the dividend. The company’s shares will trade ex-dividend on November 12. Due to the T+1 settlement system in place on the stock market, investors must purchase shares by November 11th to receive the dividend. This means that if you want to take advantage of this dividend, Wednesday, November 11th, is the last day. Investors who purchase shares after this date will not be eligible for this dividend.
The company will pay an interim dividend of ₹19 per eligible share. Therefore, the more shares you own, the greater the dividend amount.
This amount is before tax. The company has set the dividend payment date as November 25, 2026. This means that eligible investors will receive the dividend on this date.

HUL has a consistent dividend record. In fiscal year 2025-26, the company paid a total dividend of ₹41 per share, including an interim dividend of ₹19 and a final dividend of ₹22. Meanwhile, in the financial year 2024-25, the company paid a total dividend of ₹43 per share. This included an interim dividend of ₹19 and a final dividend of ₹24.

Is fermented food Asia’s next big GLP-1 opportunity? Unilever ex-R&D lead shares her take
sum: Banerjee was speaking to NutraIngredients at the recent Asia-Pacific Agri-Food Innovation Summit held in Singapore last month, where GLP-1 was one of the main topics, with Banerjee leading a roundtable discussion on “Health & Wellness: Is GLP-1 really the big opportunity in Asia?”
In the West, the popularity of GLP-1 medications has led to a new wave of opportunities for dietary supplement and food and beverage innovation.
Most innovations center on companion foods rich in protein and fiber, or portion control, where each serving has fewer calories, sugar, or sodium.
These innovations have also given rise to trends such as “fibermaxxing” or the “proteinification of everything” in the past year.
While most Asian markets have now embraced protein-rich products, the trend of fibermaxxing and portion control is still in its early days in the region, Banerjee said.
“We in Asia are following the trends; we are not driving and leading the trends,” said Banerjee, founder and director of Bangalore-based food and nutrition consultancy Thinking Forks Consulting.
However, one niche area where Asian companies can tap into to pioneer a new wave of GLP-1 nutrition innovation is fermented foods and beverages.

sum: Quality Assessment: Strong Fundamentals Amidst Flat Performance

HUL continues to demonstrate robust long-term fundamental strength, which remains a key pillar supporting the upgrade. The company boasts an impressive average Return on Equity (ROE) of 21.35%, underscoring efficient capital utilisation over time. This figure is further bolstered by a recent ROE of 24.8%, reflecting sustained profitability despite a challenging macroeconomic environment.

Net sales have grown at a steady annual rate of 6.52%, signalling consistent demand for HUL’s diverse product portfolio. Additionally, the company remains net-debt free, a significant advantage in an industry where leverage can amplify risks during downturns. Institutional investors hold a substantial 26.38% stake, indicating confidence from sophisticated market participants who typically conduct rigorous fundamental analysis.

HUL’s market capitalisation stands at ₹4,64,044 crores, making it the largest entity in the FMCG sector and accounting for 27.09% of the sector’s total market cap. Valuation remains a mixed picture for HUL. The stock trades at a price-to-book (P/B) ratio of 9.5, which is considered expensive, especially when juxtaposed with its peers. sum: Tempsens Instruments shares surged 17% on Tuesday, 3 November, extending their strong post-listing rally. The stock has gained around 89% over its IPO price of ₹300 in just over two months since its listing on 28 August 2026.

The temperature-sensing and heating solutions provider made a stellar debut on the stock exchanges, closing its listing day at a 95.6% premium over the issue price. The stock opened at ₹631.20 on the BSE, up 110.4% from its IPO price, and touched an intraday high of ₹635, representing a gain of 111.66%. It eventually settled at ₹586.80.

Last week, the company reported strong revenue growth in Q2 FY27, with consolidated revenue from operations rising 34% year-on-year to ₹136.31 crore. Revenue also increased 14.8% sequentially, supported by healthy demand across its three business verticals and the consolidation of recently acquired European entities.
For the first half of FY27, revenue grew 33.7% year-on-year to ₹255.02 crore.

However, the company's EBITDA margin contracted to 21.2% in H1 FY27 from 25.2% in the corresponding period last year, reflecting higher operating costs linked to capacity expansion and international acquisitions.
EBITDA increased 8.6% year-on-year to ₹28.32 crore in Q2 FY27, while adjusted profit after tax (PAT) rose 18.5% to ₹20.28 crore.

sum: Reliance Industries shares surged nearly 12% to ₹1,300 on Monday, their biggest comparable daily gain since April 2020, after the company reported record second-quarter profit. The rally added ₹1.84 lakh crore to its market value, lifting it to ₹17.6 lakh crore.

The shares finished Monday’s trade with a solid 12% jump to settle at ₹1,300 on NSE, their highest level since early September. The stock last posted a comparable single-day surge in April 2020. Given its heavyweight status in the Nifty 50, the rally also lifted the index by 1.7%, even as tensions in West Asia remained elevated.

For long-term Reliance Industries shareholders, the sharp rise has revived confidence in the stock, which had been trending lower since the start of 2026. The shares closed in the red in eight of the previous 10 months. Despite Monday’s rebound, the stock remains down 17.22% so far this year.

The double-digit jump in the stock added ₹1.84 lakh crore to the company’s market capitalisation, taking it to ₹17.6 lakh crore and helping it retain its position as India’s most valuable listed company.

At its peak of ₹1,611, the company commanded a market capitalisation of ₹21.8 lakh crore. It had crossed the ₹21 lakh crore mark in June 2024, becoming the first Indian company to achieve this milestone.

Meanwhile, investors in the Reliance Group have another reason to celebrate, as its telecom arm, Jio Platforms, made a blockbuster stock market debut last week, listing at ₹1,440 apiece, a premium of 21.3% over its issue price.

Reliance Industries Ltd reported a record consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of ₹29,550 crore for the July-September quarter (Q2 FY27), marking a 33.8% increase from ₹22,092 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue rose 27.8% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹3,62,268 crore, while EBITDA increased 23.9% to a record ₹62,409 crore.

Jio Platforms vs Bharti Airtel shares: Which telecom stock to buy after Reliance arm’s IPO listing? Experts suggestions
sum: The listing of Jio Platforms has put the spotlight on India’s telecom sector, with investors now weighing whether the newly listed Reliance Industries-backed company or established rival Bharti Airtel offers a better investment opportunity.

Jio Platforms shares have surged nearly 28% from their issue price of ₹1,119 since making their market debut on Wednesday, 28 October, taking its market capitalisation to nearly ₹13.18 lakh crore and making it India’s second-most valuable listed company after Reliance Industries. The strong debut and subsequent gains follow an IPO that attracted bids for 22.19 times the shares on offer.

Bharti Airtel, meanwhile, has built a strong long-term track record, with its shares delivering returns of 586.10% over the past decade and 187.07% over five years. However, the stock remains down 6.64% so far in 2026. With Jio commanding a substantial valuation and Airtel offering an established earnings track record, which telecom stock should investors consider now? Experts weigh in on their growth prospects, valuations and investment appeal.

Bharti Airtel, meanwhile, remains a stronger proposition for investors seeking earnings visibility, higher ARPU, robust cash flows and disciplined capital allocation. Experts say investors should weigh valuations, earnings growth and execution risks before choosing between the two telecom stocks.

Gaurav Arora, Head of Research at SAHI, said Jio’s listing at a valuation of around ₹10.3 lakh crore places it among India’s top five companies by market capitalisation from day one. This, he said, changes the investment question from assessing the company’s growth potential to evaluating the returns investors can realistically expect from current levels. Companies of this scale rarely grow significantly faster than the broader economy, making low double-digit annual returns a reasonable base case.

He also noted that ARPU growth in India has historically been uneven, with increases largely coming through tariff hikes in 2019, 2021 and 2024. These hikes have typically required coordinated moves by all three telecom operators and have depended on regulatory considerations, making it difficult to factor in consistent ARPU growth over a 10-year investment horizon.

items.t: Hindustan Unilever stock backs proposed nutrition labels
sum: Hindustan Unilever said it supports India's proposed front-of-pack nutrition labels and would comply with the rules once they are finalized. ChiniMandi reported the comments on October 29, 2026, citing remarks by Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Priya Nair after the company's earnings briefing.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has proposed prominent front-of-pack warnings for products high in added sugar, saturated fat or salt. The proposed labels are intended to make nutritional risks easier for consumers to identify, with implementation planned in phases to give manufacturers time to adapt.

For Hindustan Unilever, the issue is concentrated in its packaged-food and beverage portfolio, which includes Kissan, Knorr, Hellmann's, Horlicks and Boost. Clearer labeling could increase the importance of product formulation, packaging changes and consumer communication across those brands.

Chief Financial Officer Niranjan Gupta said the company regularly reviews how to deploy balance-sheet resources. He cited capital spending, acquisitions and shareholder returns as possible uses of cash, but did not confirm a specific share buyback proposal.

That leaves dividends and other capital-allocation measures as separate issues from the nutrition-labeling proposal. Investors will likely focus on how the final rules affect product positioning, reformulation costs and demand in the foods business.

Hindustan Unilever operates in India's fast-moving consumer goods market, with businesses spanning beauty and wellbeing, personal care, home care and foods. Its portfolio includes more than 50 brands serving Indian households through products such as personal-care goods, cleaning products, foods and nutrition drinks. The company competes with Procter & Gamble Hygiene & Health Care, Godrej Consumer Products and Jyothy Laboratories, while its broader portfolio gives it a different mix from those more focused rivals.
Indian consumer-goods shares remain the wider market backdrop for investors following Hindustan Unilever. Current market reports provide broader context on Indian equities.

sum: Mumbai, Oct 6 (IANS) Less than two weeks after its stock market debut, shares of the National Stock Exchange (NSE) have slipped below their initial public offering (IPO) price, wiping out all listing-day gains and reducing the exchange's market value by nearly Rs 41,000 crore from its peak.
NSE shares were listed on the BSE at Rs 1,800 apiece on September 24, a modest premium of less than 1 per cent over the IPO price of Rs 1,785.

sum: Value retailers are seeing their stocks fall sharply amid expectations of a muted second quarter, as restrained consumer spending and inflation weigh on sales growth.
On Monday, DMart-operator Avenue Supermarts Ltd fell 6.67%, while V2 Retail Ltd plunged 16.63% and Vishal Mega Mart Ltd declined 1.26%. Trent Ltd slipped 0.86%, while V-Mart Retail Ltd gained 3.19%.
The weakness reflects growing investor anxiety that higher prices and softer demand could squeeze the value-retailers’ core proposition just as the festive season gets underway.
Avenue Supermarts fell despite a strong September-quarter showing. It reported a revenue of ₹19,206.18 crore, up 18.4% year-on-year and 4.7% quarter-on-quarter, while its store count rose to 518.

Sandeep Abhange, research analyst for consumer and midcaps at financial services firm LKP Securities, said he did not see any major negatives in DMart’s update. “I thought the update was good overall,” he said.
The broader concern, he added, was the outlook for value retailers as inflation and higher costs make consumers more cautious.

Abhange expects the value-retail segment to have a muted Q2 FY27, with festive spending happening gradually rather than in a broad-based surge. “It is like it's in bits and pieces,” he said. “If someone wants it, then they are taking, but it's not like across the board.” Consumers are becoming “more cautious” even as the festive season gets underway.

HUL stock: When a great business becomes overpriced
sum: Summary: HUL is a business most of us trust without thinking twice. But trusting the business and paying any price for the stock are two different things, and this piece uses HUL's own numbers to show exactly where that line sits.

Look around your kitchen or bathroom and you'll probably spot a Hindustan Unilever product: Surf, Lux, Dove, Brooke Bond, Horlicks, you name it. You don't need to read an annual report to know this business. It's exactly the kind of company Peter Lynch told investors to look for.
But knowing a company is good is only half the job. The other half is what you pay for it.

Legendary investor Rakesh Jhunjhunwala once explained why companies like HUL trade at a premium. They grow steadily, earn high returns and hand cash back to shareholders, unlike heavy-industry businesses that keep asking for more money.
Later, he used HUL to make the opposite point. Its price ran so far ahead that the stock barely moved for close to a decade, even though the business kept performing well.
Both things were true at once. A good business deserves a premium. But even a good business can be priced too high.
Here's HUL's story in one line: over the long run, profit grew at roughly 11 per cent a year. That's solid for a mature consumer company, yet nothing extraordinary.

sum: Shares of non-banking financial company (NBFC) Paisalo Digital were locked in the 20% upper circuit in Wednesday's trade, July 1, hitting ₹71 apiece after the company announced a further increase in promoter shareholding, reinforcing confidence in its long-term growth prospects.

The promoter group acquired an additional 4.97% stake during the June quarter, taking its holding to 46.72% in Q1FY27. The latest increase marks another milestone in a consistent multi-year trend of promoter buying.
Promoter shareholding has steadily risen from around 26% in FY19 to 37% in FY25, 41.75% in FY26, and now 46.72%.

"This sustained commitment reflects the promoters' deep alignment with the company's long-term strategy and their continued confidence in Paisalo's business model, governance standards, execution capabilities, and mission of delivering responsible, technology-enabled credit to MSMEs, micro-enterprises, and underserved borrowers across Bharat," the company said in its regulatory filing.

Paisalo has outlined a three-year roadmap to double its assets under management (AUM), total income, and profit after tax (PAT) while maintaining disciplined risk management and best-in-class asset quality.

A key pillar of this strategy is the company's transition from a "High Touch–High Tech" model to a "Fin AI"-driven lending platform, integrating artificial intelligence across customer acquisition, underwriting, risk assessment, portfolio monitoring, and collections.

Commenting on the development, Santanu Agarwal, Deputy Managing Director of Paisalo Digital, said the increase in promoter shareholding to 46.72%, including the additional 4.97% stake acquired during the quarter, reflects the promoters' long-term confidence in the company's growth journey.

Multibagger stock Elitecon International share price hit its 5% upper circuit at ₹45.68 on BSE on Monday, April 20, after it announced that its equity shares commenced trading on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) with effect from April 20, 2026. With this development, all 15,98,500,000 fully paid-up equity shares of the company, with a face value of ₹1 each, are now available for trading on both exchanges, significantly broadening investor reach and improving liquidity in the stock.

Commenting on the development, Managing Director Vipin Sharma said, “The commencement of trading of our shares on NSE is an important milestone for Elitecon and our shareholders. Foods delivered 6% USG, driven by high-single-digit UVG across categories. sum: The shares of Hindustan Unilever (HUL) adjusted to the demerger of its ice-cream business, Kwality Wall's (India) on December 5. After a special pre-open session, the stock was discovered at Rs 2,422 apiece.

This is nearly 2 percent lower that its previous closing price of Rs 2,462.20 apiece. After opening, the stock sharply fell around 7 percent to hit a low of Rs 2,286.70 per share. The stock then recovered some losses to close at Rs 2,341 per share.

Earlier in November 2024, HUL approved the demerger of the ice cream business, which operates popular brands including 'Kwality Wall's', 'Cornetto' and 'Magnum'. National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) approved the demerger scheme on October 30.
The ice cream business forms 3 percent of HUL's total yearly turnover, contributing Rs 1,800 crore to the total revenue.
ICICI securities said that the ice cream business will likely be valued at Rs 9,500 crore ($1.06 billion) to Rs 11,900 crore. It values per share of the upcoming demerged entity at Rs 40-50.

The share entitlement ratio has been set at 1:1. This means that every shareholder of HUL will receive one share of the ice cream business for every share of the FMCG major they own, as on the record date

The allotment date was fixed at December 29. The record date to determine the eligibility of the shareholders set to receive the free shares was set on December 5. This means that those HUL shareholders whose names appear in the register of members as on the record date will be entitled to receive free shares of KWIL as part of the demerger.
